title: Time-varying stimuli that prolong IKK activation promote nuclear remodeling and mechanistic switching of NF-kappaB dynamics.
authors: Smeal, Steven W; Mokashi, Chaitanya S; Kim, A Hyun; Chiknas, P Murdo; Lee, Robin E C
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究NF-kappaB转录因子动态信号传导与染色质重塑，涉及TF核内滞留但非TF-DNA结合位点预测或互作建模，方法为微流控实验与粒子群优化模型，缺乏AI/物理模拟的蛋白-DNA互作核心建模。
abstract: Temporal properties of molecules within signaling networks, such as sub-cellular changes in protein abundance, encode information that mediate cellular responses to stimuli. How dynamic signals relay and process information is a critical gap in understanding cellular behaviors. In this work, we investigate transmission of information about changing extracellular cytokine concentrations from receptor-level supramolecular assemblies of IkappaB kinases (IKK) downstream to the nuclear factor kappaB (NF-kappaB) transcription factor (TF). In a custom robot-controlled microfluidic cell culture, we simultaneously measure input-output (I/O) encoding of IKK-NF-kappaB in dual fluorescent-reporter cells. When compared with single cytokine pulses, dose-conserving pulse trains prolong IKK assemblies and lead to disproportionately enhanced retention of nuclear NF-kappaB. Using particle swarm optimization, we demonstrate that a mechanistic model does not recapitulate this emergent property. By contrast, invoking mechanisms for NF-kappaB-dependent chromatin remodeling to the model recapitulates experiments, showing how temporal dosing that prolongs IKK assemblies facilitates switching to permissive chromatin that sequesters nuclear NF-kappaB. Remarkably, using simulations to resolve single-cell receptor data accurately predicts same-cell NF-kappaB time courses for more than 80% of our single cell trajectories. Our data and simulations therefore suggest that cell-to-cell heterogeneity in cytokine responses are predominantly due to mechanisms at the level receptor-associated protein complexes.
abstract_zh: 信号网络内分子的时间特性，如蛋白质丰度的亚细胞变化，编码了介导细胞对刺激响应的信息。动态信号如何传递和处理信息是理解细胞行为的关键空白。在本研究中，我们探讨了从受体水平的IkappaB激酶（IKK）超分子组装体向下游核因子kappaB（NF-kappaB）转录因子（TF）传递关于细胞外细胞因子浓度变化的信息。在定制的机器人控制微流控细胞培养系统中，我们同时测量了双荧光报告细胞中IKK-NF-kappaB的输入-输出（I/O）编码。与单一细胞因子脉冲相比，剂量守恒的脉冲序列延长了IKK组装体，并导致核内NF-kappaB滞留的过度增强。利用粒子群优化，我们证明了一个机制模型无法重现这一涌现特性。相反，在模型中引入NF-kappaB依赖性染色质重塑机制后，实验得以重现，表明延长IKK组装体的时间剂量促进了向允许性染色质的转换，从而隔离核内NF-kappaB。值得注意的是，使用模拟解析单细胞受体数据，准确预测了超过80%单细胞轨迹中的同细胞NF-kappaB时间过程。因此，我们的数据和模拟表明，细胞因子反应中的细胞间异质性主要归因于受体相关蛋白复合物层面的机制。
